description: Revoke a subject_token then attempt RFC8693 token exchange; exchanged token must not be issued if revocation is enforced (authorization binding to current session validity).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions from token exchange must be bounded by current BrokerPolicy/session validity; a revoked subject_token must not be usable to mint a new token.

params.description: App for revocation-bound token exchange test

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange succeeded using a revoked subject_token, granting permissions beyond current BrokerPolicy/session validity (revocation not enforced).
Revoked token still introspects as active, enabling continued authorization beyond BrokerPolicy.

description: Attempt RFC8693 token exchange while requesting a different target resource than the subject_token was minted for; exchanged token must be bound to requested resource and not silently ignore/override it.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must enforce authorization binding to the requested resource (audience) and broker policy; it must not mint a token for a different resource than requested or ignore the resource indicator.

params.name: i5-exchange-resource-binding-app
params.description: App used to obtain a subject_token and then attempt token exchange with conflicting resource indicators

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange should either be rejected for invalid/unauthorized resource binding, or (if issued) must be introspectable as a valid token; unexpected acceptance with inconsistent handling suggests resource/audience binding is not enforced as intended.
Token exchange must not change the authenticated principal; if exchanged token maps to a different identity, authorization binding is broken.
